capstones.label: Published written analysis
capstones.blurb: A piece of analytical writing on a real question, put in front of people who could disagree with it.
capstones.evidencePrompt: Link or attach the piece, and name where it was published or who read it.

rubric.label: The central claim is stated plainly and is falsifiable
Evidence is weighted rather than merely cited
The strongest counterargument is engaged, not caricatured
A reader can reconstruct the argument from the structure alone
Uncertainty is stated where it exists, without hedging everything

capstones.label: Solved problem from an unfamiliar domain
capstones.blurb: A genuinely novel problem, solved from outside your usual field, with the approach documented as it happened.
capstones.evidencePrompt: Attach the working, including the approaches that failed and why you abandoned them.

rubric.label: The problem was genuinely unfamiliar, not a variant of one you had solved
The decomposition is explicit and the parts were independently solvable
Failed approaches are recorded with the reason they were dropped
The solution was checked by something other than your own satisfaction

capstones.label: Taught to competence
capstones.blurb: Someone else can now do the thing, unaided, because of you.
capstones.evidencePrompt: Describe what the learner could do afterwards that they could not do before, and how you know.

rubric.label: The learner's starting point was established before you began
The final demonstration was unaided and delayed by at least a day
The explanation changed in response to what they did not understand
They could apply it to a case you had not covered

capstones.label: Thirty scored predictions
capstones.blurb: A resolved forecasting record with a calibration curve. The strongest objective evidence available in this system.
capstones.evidencePrompt: Neuron computes this from your resolved predictions. Add a note on what your calibration curve shows.

rubric.label: At least thirty predictions, resolved on their stated dates
Probabilities span the range rather than clustering at 50%
The Brier decomposition shows resolution, not just calibration
Ambiguous outcomes were called at the time, not retrofitted

capstones.label: Pre-registered experiment with a reported null
capstones.blurb: A real comparison you ran, reported as it came out — including if it came out against you.
capstones.evidencePrompt: Attach the pre-registration and the result, in that order, with timestamps.

rubric.label: The analysis was specified before the data existed
The sample size was justified rather than convenient
The main confounders were identified and addressed or acknowledged
The result is reported as it came out, with its uncertainty

capstones.label: Negotiation with a pre-registered target
capstones.blurb: A real negotiation where you wrote your reservation value and target down beforehand.
capstones.evidencePrompt: Record the pre-written target and reservation value, then what actually happened.

rubric.label: Target, reservation value and alternatives were written before the conversation
The other side's underlying interests were identified, not just their position
You stayed on strategy when it became uncomfortable
The relationship is intact and you would negotiate with them again

capstones.label: Shipped project with an iteration log
capstones.blurb: Something real, finished and in front of users, with the cycles documented.
capstones.evidencePrompt: Link the finished thing and attach the log of what each cycle changed and why.

rubric.label: It is finished and in front of someone other than you
Each cycle changed the next version in response to real feedback
Something good was cut, on stated criteria
The final scope is defensible against the original plan

capstones.label: Research synthesis in an unfamiliar field
capstones.blurb: A summary of what is known and disputed in a field you did not know three weeks ago.
capstones.evidencePrompt: Attach the synthesis and, if you can, a reaction from someone who works in that field.

rubric.label: The field's main results and main disagreement are correctly identified
Sources are weighted by evidence quality rather than by prominence
What could not be resolved is stated explicitly
Someone who works in the field would not find it embarrassing
